transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?
I came in because most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It feels like the old me—the guy who could talk to anybody and enjoy the day—is just gone.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
About eight months now. It started when the new regional manager began coming down on me and taking away accounts I’d handled for years.
Over these past eight months, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you normally used to enjoy?
Yeah. I used to look forward to bowling, gardening, taking my wife to gallery shows, even going dancing. Now I just make excuses and sit at home. None of it feels worth the effort anymore.
Have you ever had times in your life where you felt the opposite—unusually energetic, elated, or wired, and needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I can’t think of a time like that. I haven’t really noticed myself getting unusually up or wired like you mean.
Before this started eight months ago, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt this depressed or down for weeks at a time?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another time that I felt down like this for weeks on end.
How has your sleep been over these past few months?
I lie awake replaying work and staring at the ceiling. Then when I do get to sleep, I wake up around three or four in the morning, already worn out and dreading the day.
Have you been struggling with feeling worthless or blaming yourself excessively for things lately?
Yeah. I keep telling myself I’m useless now. All those years taking care of clients and providing for my family, it feels like none of it counts because I can’t even handle this job anymore.
With everything feeling so heavy and useless, have you had any thoughts of wanting to end your life or that you would be better off dead?
...Yes. I’ve been thinking that my wife and kids might be better off if I just didn’t wake up. It scares me, honestly. I don’t trust myself the way I used to.
